This wasn't an option, so I'm writing it. Short answer: depends. Long answer: Thanks to brigading, timezones, lurkers, and the general unreliableness of online polling, probably not. If I were sure the polling were actually indicative of the majority, probably. It's hard enough to even get people to participate.

This is complicated. If I modded a popular community with other mods who are not being called to step down, then I would likely listen to the community's opinion and those of my fellow mods and weigh the situation as fairly as possible. If the majority opinion is for me to step down, then I would.

Now if I am the sole mod of a small community and are being called to step down, then I would try to find a common ground with the community instead. Not having a backup mod to take over and having the community call for my dismissal would mean I somehow either screwed up big time and need to make amends, or I am being trolled. Because the latter is a possibility, I would not simply bow to the shouting masses. Small subs that are for niche content should never really run into this discourse in the first place, so it seems the coup would be nothing more than a land/power grab.

If my continued modship is negatively affecting the community then yes. If it is just people who don't like me then no.

I think the argument is whether this situation falls into category one or category two.
I would step down if someone gave a good argument for why I shouldn't moderate. If it's just a large number of people who don't like me or disagree with established rules then I would never give in.
